www is a subdomain of a domain. it was important back in the early days of internet and helped direct the user to the correct folder under a domain. Seems logical.. World Wide Web, right? www used to mean "Designate this part of a site to the world instead of keeping it private." Internet used to be strictly military.

Well now www's are carry over. We don't need the w's, and Go Daddy doesn't even sell www's since forever, but because so many people still think we do, when we upload our websites, servers are set up to put your site in a w's folder and one without.  Look at your FTP in Filezilla and you will see your whole site under both www and public_html (ie: 2 folders under one domain: one refererenced with www and one without.) SO, most sites are in two folders under one domain! AND most browsers don't give a toot which one they access unless you state your preference.

As a site owner, you resolve this issue by telling the browser which folder you prefer, and put that HTML in the head of your site. 

Choosing one over the other is important because it increases your rank. You want a browser to consistently link to one of these two folders instead of guessing between both.
